es.title: Noticias de Copyright e Inteligencia Artificial

items.title: Italian Competition Watchdog Launches Suno Investigation ‘Over Unfair Terms,’ Says ‘The Contractual Provisions on Copyright Deserve Particular Attention’
items.summary: Suno, el generador de música IA, está siendo investigado por la Autoridad de Competencia de Italia por supuestos términos contractuales injustos, con especial atención a las cláusulas de derechos de autor, mientras enfrenta varias demandas y reclamaciones internacionales de copyright.

items.title: Sony Music’s AI Slop and Deepfakes Crackdown Intensifies — Soundalike Track Removal Requests Reportedly Top 250,000
items.summary: Sony Music ha enviado más de 250,000 solicitudes de eliminación para retirar pistas generadas por IA que imitan su catálogo, incluyendo deepfakes, mostrando una campaña intensificada de protección de derechos, según informa el Financial Times.

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: Un tribunal japonés determinó que los derechos de publicidad de los artistas impiden clones de voz no autorizados por IA, mientras que un tribunal de apelaciones estadounidense rechazó la defensa de uso justo de una empresa de IA para entrenar datos, evidenciando enfoques legales diferentes.

items.title: Who Really Wrote Katy Perry’s ‘Hot N Cold’? A Bizarre Twist Could Derail a Dr. Luke Copyright Settlement In South Dakota
items.summary: Un caso de derechos de autor de Dr. Luke en Dakota del Sur avanza hacia un acuerdo, pero una tercera parte ha intervenido alegando derechos de autoría, lo que podría complicar la resolución de disputas sobre canciones como “Hot N Cold” de Katy Perry.

items.title: Major publishers tell US Supreme Court they must intervene in termination rights ruling that “threatens the licensing of copyrighted works throughout the world”
items.summary: Los principales editores musicales y BMG presentaron un escrito ante la Corte Suprema de EE. UU. solicitando intervención en un caso de derechos de terminación que involucra al compositor Cyril Vetter, alegando que la decisión podría poner en riesgo la licencia mundial de obras protegidas.

tip.title: Trabajo por encargo: quién queda como autor se pacta por escrito
tip.body: Si produces para un cliente, define por contrato si cedes derechos, si conservas puntos de producción y si tu nombre aparece en los créditos. Sin contrato, la interpretación depende de la ley de cada país.

en.title: Copyright & Artificial Intelligence News
en.subtitle: Stories published by real industry outlets, each linked to its original article. No invented news.

items.title: Italian Competition Watchdog Launches Suno Investigation ‘Over Unfair Terms,’ Says ‘The Contractual Provisions on Copyright Deserve Particular Attention’
items.summary: Suno, the AI music generator, is being investigated by Italy's Competition Authority for allegedly unfair contract terms, with particular focus on copyright provisions, as the company also faces multiple lawsuits and international copyright claims.

items.title: Sony Music’s AI Slop and Deepfakes Crackdown Intensifies — Soundalike Track Removal Requests Reportedly Top 250,000
items.summary: Sony Music has filed more than 250,000 takedown requests to remove AI‑generated soundalike tracks and deepfake recordings, reflecting an intensified effort to protect its catalog, as reported by the Financial Times.

items.title: Japanese court says voice is protected by publicity rights; US appeals court says AI training is not fair use
items.summary: A Japanese court ruled that performers’ publicity rights block unauthorized AI voice clones, while a U.S. appeals court rejected an AI company’s fair‑use defense for training data, highlighting divergent legal approaches to AI in music.

items.title: Who Really Wrote Katy Perry’s ‘Hot N Cold’? A Bizarre Twist Could Derail a Dr. Luke Copyright Settlement In South Dakota
items.summary: A Dr. Luke copyright case in South Dakota has moved toward settlement, but a third party has intervened claiming authorship rights, potentially complicating the resolution of disputes over songs such as Katy Perry’s “Hot N Cold.”

items.title: Major publishers tell US Supreme Court they must intervene in termination rights ruling that “threatens the licensing of copyrighted works throughout the world”
items.summary: Major music publishers and BMG have filed a brief with the U.S. Supreme Court urging intervention in a termination‑rights case concerning songwriter Cyril Vetter, arguing the ruling could jeopardize global licensing of copyrighted works.

tip.title: Work for hire: put authorship in writing
tip.body: If you produce for a client, spell out in the contract whether you assign rights, keep producer points, and get credited. Without a contract, the outcome depends on each country's law.
